title: Developer Experience Documentation: SDK Guides, Quickstarts, API Examples, Docs Site Ops, and Top Support Issues
author: Sofia Martinez
content:
Overview

This page centralizes standards, templates, and operating procedures for Developer Experience (DevEx) documentation at Redwood Inference. It covers the canonical structure for SDK guides, quickstarts and templates, API examples, docs-site operating procedures, and our top support issues and canonical fixes. The goal is consistent, discoverable, and high-quality docs that minimize developer friction and support load.

Audience
- DevEx writers and engineers producing public-facing documentation and SDK guides.
- Support engineers and triage owners who maintain canonical fixes.
- Product and platform engineers who consume quickstarts and samples.

Goals
1. Provide repeatable templates so every SDK guide and quickstart has the same structure and discoverability signals.
2. Ensure API examples are runnable, copy-paste friendly, and cover common integration patterns (auth, streaming, error handling).
3. Maintain a lightweight docs-site publishing workflow that enforces reviews, linting, and automated smoke tests.
4. Track and publish top support issues with canonical fixes to reduce mean time to resolution (MTTR).

Document types and canonical templates
- SDK Guide (long-form): Purpose, quickstart, API reference links, examples (sync/async), troubleshooting, upgrade notes, changelog pointer.
- Quickstart (one page): Problem statement, 5-minute setup, runnable example, expected output, next steps.
- API Example: Minimal curl + language SDK examples showing authentication, request, streaming, and error handling.
- Docs-site OPS: Publishing checklist, CI workflow, versioning policy, rollback procedure.
- Top Support Issues: Issue summary, detection signals/metrics, root cause patterns, canonical fix steps, ownership and runbook link.

SDK Guide structure (required sections)
1. Title and short description (1 sentence)
2. Use cases and recommended scenarios
3. Prerequisites (API keys, SDK versions, required permissions)
4. Quickstart (runnable, minimal example)
5. Detailed examples (sync, async, streaming, edge cases)
6. Configuration & best-practices (timeouts, batching, retries, rate limits)
7. Troubleshooting & common errors (with error codes and canonical fixes)
8. Upgrade notes and compatibility matrix
9. Ownership and links (owner, reviewers, related pages)

SDK quickstart template (5-minute guide)
- Title: SDK Quickstart — <language>
- Description: 1–2 sentences explaining the integration scenario
- Prereqs:
  - Redwood API key with dev scope
  - SDK version >= x.y.z
- Steps:
  1. Install SDK: ``pip install redwood-sdk`` (or ``npm install @redwood/inference``)
  2. Set API key: ``export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-...``
  3. Run minimal example: see snippet below
- Expected output: small JSON block or sample console output
- Next steps / Links: link to full SDK guide and API reference

Example quickstart (Python)
```
from redwood import RedwoodClient
import os
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ.get("REDWOOD_API_KEY"))
resp = client.generate(model="redwood-1-small", prompt="Translate to French: 'Hello world'")
print(resp.text)
```

curl example (API examples section)
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-1-small","input":"Summarize: Redwood Inference mission."}'
```

API examples guidelines
- Every example must include a curl + at least two language SDKs (Python, JavaScript).
- Show auth, request body, headers, and expected response.
- Include a streaming example (server-sent events or chunked transfer) where applicable.
- Add a short troubleshooting subsection for common 4xx/5xx responses and their canonical remediation.
- Mark deprecated fields and provide migration examples.

Docs site operating procedures (publisher playbook)
- Branching and edits:
  - Content changes must be made in the docs repo (docs/) on a topic branch named docs/<area>/<short-desc>.
  - Small fixes (typos, formatting) may use the docs/fixes branch with a concise PR description.
- PR checklist (required):
  1. Title and one-line summary at top of page.
  2. Add metadata frontmatter: title, author, created_at, last_updated, labels, related_pages.
  3. Lint: run ``./scripts/docs-lint`` and fix warnings.
  4. Link-check: run ``./scripts/verify-links``.
  5. Smoke test examples: run ``./scripts/run-examples`` — confirm examples succeed in CI.
  6. Assign at least one reviewer from DevEx (owner team).
  7. Add reviewers and add the PR to the docs release milestone.
- CI publishing steps (automated):
  1. PR merged to main triggers docs CI: build -> spellcheck -> example smoke test -> deploy to staging.
  2. Staging smoke tests run nightly; a post is created if any smoke test fails.
  3. Manual approval in staging required for production deploy (release owner).
- Rollback procedure:
  1. Revert PR that introduced the broken content.
  2. Rebuild and deploy from main.
  3. Notify #docs-alerts with revert summary and related issue.

Docs metadata frontmatter standard (YAML example)
```
---
title: "SDK Quickstart — Python"
author: "Sofia Martinez"
created_at: "2026-03-15"
last_updated: "2026-11-15"
labels: ["sdk","quickstart","python"]
related_pages: ["/confluence/eng-developer-experience/quickstarts-and-templates/developer-experience-sdk-quickstarts-api-examples-2026.json"]
---
```

Top support issues and canonical fixes (triage & KB)
- Purpose: keep a living, prioritized list of high-frequency support tickets with a verified canonical fix that support and oncall can apply quickly. Maintain a runbook link for each issue.
- Ownership: Support Triage team owns accuracy; DevEx owns the KB content; the service owner is tagged for long-term fixes.

Top issues (examples and canonical fixes)
1) Auth failures for new customers (401/403)
   - Detection: spike in 401s for a single customer, error rate > 5% of requests for that API key in 10m window.
   - Common root causes: expired key, wrong environment variable, missing project scope.
   - Canonical fix:
     - Verify API key in customer portal and permissions.
     - CLI check: ``curl -I -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" https://api.redwood.dev/v1/status``
     - If key expired: rotate and instruct customer to update env vars.
   - Runbook: /confluence/support/runbooks/auth-key-rotation

2) High tail latency for streaming responses
   - Detection: p95 latency > 500ms for streaming endpoints, correlated to a single model or region.
   - Root cause patterns: Batch scheduling misconfiguration, KV cache warmup, model variant fallback.
   - Canonical fix:
     - Verify routing config and batching policy for affected tenant in the console.
     - Temporarily route traffic to a lower-latency model variant: update route policy in console or via API.
     - Ensure KV cache warmup by replaying representative prefixes in staging.
   - Runbook: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runbooks/streaming-latency-triage

3) Model error: "context length exceeded" (413)
   - Detection: persistent 413 responses, user-visible truncation reports.
   - Root cause: client sending unexpectedly long prompts or log accumulation in prefix cache.
   - Canonical fix:
     - Educate user to chunk input or use embeddings + retrieval pattern.
     - Update client-side validation to calculate token length before submit.
     - Provide sample code snippet to pre-check token length (Python).

4) SDK mismatch causing unexpected exceptions after a patch
   - Detection: spikes in support tickets after SDK release, reproducible with specific SDK versions.
   - Canonical fix:
     - Confirm SDK version matrix in release notes.
     - Provide quick compatibility patch or rollback instructions.
     - Ensure SDK installer pins compatible transitive deps.

5) Rate-limit (429) for bursty workloads
   - Detection: high 429 rate across tenant routes; alerts firing on error budget usage.
   - Canonical fix:
     - Recommend client-side retry/backoff with jitter (RFC 6585 pattern).
     - For persistent throughput needs, escalate to Dedicated capacity recommendation.

(Additional issues 6–10: malformed JSON payloads, streaming disconnects, embedding mismatches, billing metadata missing, and incorrect model selection; full KB is maintained in the support-runbooks directory.)

Canonical fixes verification and publishing flow
1. Support engineer crafts a KB entry with reproduction steps and a verified fix in a staging tenant.
2. Add the KB entry as a page under /confluence/support and link to the DevEx quickstart or SDK guide where relevant.
3. Peer review by DevEx and a sign-off from the owning service team.
4. After publication, add the KB to the weekly support sync agenda for 2 cycles to gather feedback.

Monitoring and SLOs for docs-driven issues
- Example metrics to monitor:
  - Docs example smoke test failures (count per week) — target 0/week
  - Docs link-check failures (daily) — target 0/day
  - Number of tickets referencing "example doesn't run" — target decrease by 50% after remediation
  - Time-to-first-fix for top-10 KB items — target < 72h

Ownership and escalation
- DevEx lead: Sofia Martinez (primary owner for docs quality and operating procedures).
- Support Triage: Marcus Chen (owner for KB accuracy and triage).
- Eng serving/runtime owner: Elena Novak (owner for performance-related KB and runbooks).
- Escalation path: Support -> DevEx -> Service Owner -> Eng oncall.

Publishing checklist (TL;DR)
- Add metadata frontmatter
- Run lint and link-check scripts
- Smoke-test examples in CI
- Assign DevEx reviewer and merge to main
- Monitor staging smoke tests and approve for production

Appendix: Useful commands and scripts
- Lint docs: ``./scripts/docs-lint``
- Verify links: ``./scripts/verify-links``
- Run examples locally: ``./scripts/run-examples --filter <file>``
- Publish staging (CI): merge PR and wait for staging deploy; for manual deploy: ``./scripts/deploy-staging``
